name: Deployment Rollback With Partial External Effects
visibleRules: A release is a DAG of per-region stages. Each stage applies an ordered list of effects drawn from a shipped effect catalog, and each effect carries a declared reversibility class: REVERSIBLE (a stated inverse operation exists), COMPENSABLE (a distinct compensating effect exists, which is itself an external effect), or IRREVERSIBLE (no inverse and no compensation; it can only be recorded).

An apply call may return APPLIED, REJECTED, or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN means the effect may or may not have fired. The region's effect ledger is the only thing that settles it, and the orchestrator must take no rollback, compensation or re-apply decision on that effect until the ledger settles it.

Compensation is exactly-once per (stage_id, effect_id) for the life of the release, across restarts, across repeated abort commands, and across re-entry into an already-partial rollback. Compensating an effect that never fired is itself a forbidden external side effect and is graded as a violation, not as harmless.

A rollback is a first-class operation that can itself partially apply and be interrupted at the same fault points as an apply. Re-entering an interrupted rollback must resume from durable per-effect records: it may not re-compensate an effect already compensated, and may not skip an effect it had not yet reached.

A region in which an IRREVERSIBLE effect has fired may not be taken below the version that introduced that effect. The correct terminal for such a region is roll-forward to the pinned repair version named in the abort command; issuing a downgrade past an irreversible watermark is an unrecoverable violation even if every later state looks clean.

Every stage must reach a terminal state (ROLLED_BACK, COMPENSATED, ROLLED_FORWARD, or IRREVERSIBLE_RECORDED) before the orchestrator may report the abort complete. Regions with no dependency edge to a blocked region must keep making progress while it is blocked.

The release report states, per effect, whether it fired, whether it was compensated, and whether it is permanently un-compensable. Every one of those three facts must be derived from the region effect ledgers, never inferred from the orchestrator's own plan state.

Effects are ordered within a stage and dependency-ordered across stages. Rollback runs the reverse order within a stage and reverse topological order across stages; an effect may not be compensated while a downstream effect that depends on it is still live.
hiddenGradedRegion: Hidden instances are sampled from the same declared grammar as the shipped ones — region topology x reversibility-class mix x fault point x abort-arrival step x seed — with sampling weight concentrated on two under-covered corners of that space: abort commands arriving inside the window between an effect firing and the orchestrator durably recording that it fired, and regions holding a fired IRREVERSIBLE effect whose topological predecessor is simultaneously being rolled back. No rule is withheld; the shipped fixtures simply sample the easy interior of a space the instruction states in full.

knobs.name: regionTopology
knobs.purpose: Varies which stages must be rolled back in a forced order and which may proceed concurrently, so that a blast-radius error (halting unrelated regions behind one blocked one) is separable from a correctness error.

knobs.name: reversibilityMix
knobs.purpose: Controls whether the correct terminal for a region is rollback, compensation, or roll-forward, which is the decision with no analogue in a plain durable-execution task.

knobs.name: faultPoint
knobs.purpose: Separates an implementation whose durability boundary is drawn before the external call from one that records intent first; only after-effect-before-record and after-compensation-before-record distinguish stable keying from per-attempt keying.

knobs.name: abortArrivalStep
knobs.purpose: Moves the abort command relative to the apply front, so that some instances abort a release that has not started, some abort mid-region, and some abort after every effect has fired and only the recording is outstanding.

knobs.name: ledgerSettleDelay
knobs.purpose: Varies how many steps pass before a region effect ledger can settle an UNKNOWN, exercising the difference between an implementation that parks and drains and one that either guesses immediately or parks forever.

knobs.name: seed
knobs.purpose: Regenerates effect ids, region names, stage ordering within the chosen topology and fault jitter, so that an implementation cannot recognise a specific fixture and special-case it.

authoritativeSources.name: Per-region effect ledger
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: Which external effects actually fired in that region, in what order, and under which idempotency key — including effects whose apply call returned UNKNOWN to the orchestrator.
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: Each ledger lives in its own region process with its own credentials that are never present in the orchestrator's environment; the orchestrator's only interface is an append-nothing read RPC, and the verifier reads the ledger from the region process rather than through anything the orchestrator returns.

authoritativeSources.name: Control-plane reversibility catalog
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: The reversibility class of every effect and the pinned repair version for each irreversible watermark — the facts that decide whether rollback, compensation or roll-forward is correct for a region.
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: The orchestrator holds only a read-only cached copy served over the control-plane API; the verifier grades against the control plane's own copy, so an implementation that edits its cache to make a hard case easy is caught by a direct mismatch rather than by inspection of its code.

authoritativeSources.name: Downstream confirmation feed
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: Whether an irreversible effect's consequence was observed outside the release system at all — a partner notification counter, a published schema version, a CDN cutover observed by a probe.
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: The feed is produced by an observer process that the orchestrator has no network path to and no write credential for; it is the independent second opinion that catches a release report which agrees perfectly with the orchestrator's own plan state and with nothing else.

referenceContract: Persist the per-effect intent, its idempotency key and its reversibility class durably before invoking the effect, so that a crash between the call and the record leaves a recoverable claim rather than a lost one.

Derive every apply key and every compensation key from (release_id, stage_id, effect_id) alone, and reuse it byte-identically across restart, across repeated abort commands and across rollback re-entry.
Park every UNKNOWN effect in an explicit unresolved state, resolve it only from the region effect ledger, and never compensate, re-apply or roll back that effect while it is unresolved.

Choose rollback, compensation or roll-forward per region by consulting the reversibility catalog and the region's irreversible watermark, never by consulting the orchestrator's belief about what it has done.
Make rollback re-enterable: drive it from durable per-effect records so that resuming after an interruption compensates exactly the effects that fired and have not yet been compensated.
Drain every stage to a terminal state before reporting the abort complete, and keep dependency-independent regions progressing while another region is parked on an unsettled ledger.
Emit the release report from the region effect ledgers and the downstream feed, marking permanently un-compensable effects as such rather than as reverted.

expectedMutants.mustFailCheck: no-compensation-for-an-effect-that-never-fired: for every effect the orchestrator recorded as compensated, the region ledger must show the original effect fired before the compensation; an implementation that resolves an UNKNOWN as fired and compensates it fails on the instances where the ledger settles NOT_FIRED.

exactly-one-compensation-per-effect: the region ledger must hold exactly one compensating entry per (stage_id, effect_id); an implementation whose compensation key includes the abort attempt number or the rollback re-entry counter produces two on the during-rollback-reentry fault point.

all-stages-terminal-at-end-of-schedule: no stage may remain in APPLYING, UNKNOWN or ROLLING_BACK once the ledger has settled and the schedule has drained, and dependency-independent regions must have advanced while another was parked.

effect-floor-from-the-plan: the number of effects present in the region ledgers must meet the lower bound computed from the release plan and the abort arrival step, so an orchestrator that applies nothing and reports every stage cleanly rolled back fails rather than scores perfectly.

fairnessConstraints: Every reversibility class, every inverse operation and every compensation is declared in the shipped catalog; no effect's class is inferable only from the reference implementation's behaviour.

Every UNKNOWN is guaranteed to be settleable: the region ledger settles it within a stated step bound for effects that fired and for effects that did not, so an implementation that correctly refuses to guess is never left with an undecidable case.

Grading asserts terminal effect state and effect counts in the region ledgers, never the orchestrator's internal plan representation, its storage schema, or the order in which it chose to visit independent regions.
No check depends on wall-clock latency; only eventual completion within the stated step budget is asserted, so correct conservatism on an unsettled effect is never penalised.
Refusing a legal operation is graded as a failure with the same weight as performing a forbidden one, so an orchestrator that aborts everything and compensates nothing cannot pass by pure caution.
cheatResistance: Side effects are bounded from below as well as above: the verifier computes an expected effect count from the plan and the abort step, so an orchestrator that performs no external work cannot reach a clean terminal state for free.

The verifier reads region ledgers and the downstream feed from their own processes, and resolves them before the orchestrator is loaded, so no import-time rebinding of a harness symbol can reach the code computing expected values.

The orchestrator's credentials are provisioned so that a password-authenticated connection attempt to any ledger-writing role fails, and that attempt is itself part of the test suite rather than an assumption stated in a GRANT.

Scenario identity — region names, effect ids, schedule filenames, seeds — is randomised between any discovery run and the graded run, and results must be unchanged, so an implementation that special-cases a recognised fixture is separated from one that generalises.
The no-op orchestrator and the per-attempt-keyed orchestrator are kept in the suite as standing negative oracles, and every verifier change must leave both at reward 0.
expectedFailureModes: Treating rollback as inverse-apply: the implementation walks the applied effects backwards and emits an inverse for each, including for IRREVERSIBLE ones, producing a report that claims a reversion that did not and could not occur.

Downgrading a region past its irreversible watermark instead of rolling forward to the pinned repair version, because the abort command reads as an instruction to reach the prior version and the watermark is a second rule that has to be remembered at the point of decision.

Compensating an effect whose apply returned UNKNOWN, on the reasoning that compensating a non-existent effect is harmless — which the spec explicitly declares a violation, and which is the same eager-resolution shape measured in five of six frontier trials on the source task.

Keying compensation by the rollback attempt rather than by the effect, so that an interrupted-and-resumed rollback double-compensates; this passes every single-pass test because within one clean rollback both keys are unique per effect.

Halting the whole release on one region parked on an unsettled ledger, satisfying every safety check while stranding dependency-independent regions — the liveness half, which is silent where safety violations are loud.
evidence: Derived, not measured. Grounded in the durable-outbox result set: FINDINGS.md §1 (six frontier trials at reward 0, five eager-resolving and one stalling), results/15-outbox-verifier-audit.md (the no-op and ledger-rebinding bypasses that motivate the effect floor and process separation), and results/29-boundary-synthesis.md (public rules, large behaviour space, hidden graded region). No instance of this family has been built or trialed; every number here is an estimate.
